subject.title: [Feature] Allow configuring Gemini safety settings in OpenClaw

question: Should OpenClaw expose operator-configurable Gemini safety thresholds, and which permanent configuration owner and transport scope should it use?
rationale: This adds public configuration that can deliberately relax an upstream safety control, while provider-level, per-model, Vertex, custom-endpoint, and precedence choices have materially different compatibility consequences.

options.title: Provider-owned model parameters
options.body: Use a Google-plugin-owned, validated per-model parameters contract and inject it only for explicitly supported Google transports.

options.title: Provider-level inheritance
options.body: Add a typed models.providers entry and define inheritance, custom-provider matching, request precedence, and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Keep Google defaults
options.body: Decline built-in configuration and leave altered safety policy to an external provider plugin or proxy.

recommendation.title: Provider-owned model parameters
recommendation.body: Use a Google-plugin-owned, validated per-model parameters contract and inject it only for explicitly supported Google transports.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior review routed this exact policy decision, and the available history connects this handle to both affected ownership boundaries.
